title: Installer validation exhausted local disk while unpacking npm
symptom: The full Python follow-up check failed the explicit-host installer scenario with npm TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOSPC; the filesystem had approximately 210 MiB free.

rootCause.summary: Local disk exhaustion prevented npm tar extraction. Large completed review JSONL streams from this task retained redundant uncompressed bytes; this failure is separate from the prior macOS CI child timeout.

requestedOutcome: Retain full review evidence without redundant storage, restore enough local scratch capacity, and rerun the actual installer and full check.
decisions: Compress only seven named completed logs generated by this task. Verify decompressed SHA-256 equals the original before removing its uncompressed copy.
Do not remove user data, global caches, active review streams or unrelated projects.

actions.description: Preserve the failing log and identify ENOSPC with filesystem measurement.
Losslessly archive seven completed task-owned review streams and record byte/hash evidence.
Rerun the current-source full check including the failed installer scenario.
Complete a bounded GLM transport using final text output after the JSON retry amplified cumulative output without a verdict.

verification.name: Lossless log compaction
verification.scope: Seven named completed scratch logs, no active or unrelated data.
verification.result: All decompressed SHA-256 values matched originals. Recorded net compaction was 2,478,353,741 bytes; filesystem subsequently reported about 2.8 GiB available.

verification.name: Full validation after capacity recovery
verification.scope: Current frozen runtime and strengthened regression tests.
verification.result: The full check completed with 648 passes, five pre-existing missing-parser skips, zero failures, TypeScript and shell checks. The formerly failing explicit-host npm installer scenario passed.

verification.name: GLM transport after storage recovery
verification.scope: Same requested GLM model; final text output, reduced runtime packet and bounded resource use. Source verdict remains separate from transport completion.
verification.result: The final text-mode attempt completed with exit 0, empty stderr and a 5,368-byte final response. Output SHA-256 d9a73a840e85494ac7a0682732111477cfa1cb4f616a7a6e5a2bde1ae1f3c67d. The separately scoped static source verdict was PASS with no mandatory findings; prior interrupted transports remain historical failures.

related.note: Actual npm and host-selection installation scenario.
Different failure mechanism; disk recovery does not diagnose the prior CI timeout.

history.summary: Full validation hit an npm ENOSPC extraction failure with only about 210 MiB free.
Archived seven completed task-owned streams, verified every decompressed digest, removed only redundant originals, and started full validation again.
After lossless task-log compaction and the separate obsolete corpus-test correction, full check passed including the exact installer scenario. No installer runtime change was required for ENOSPC.

The first GLM attempt also ended from the earlier disk exhaustion, with no terminal verdict. Its raw bytes were retained losslessly; a smaller request with directly compressed output is being retried after capacity recovery. Status returns to verifying for this additional affected workflow.

The directly compressed retry exceeded 1 GB and was terminated before reaching the free-space floor. Closed-pipe exit zero did not provide a final verdict. Event metadata and digest were retained; the amplified reasoning stream was removed. A bounded text-mode attempt uses the same model with a smaller runtime packet.

Full validation and the final bounded text-mode GLM transport completed. Earlier disk/stream failures remain recorded; no speculative source fix was needed for the environment failures. The GLM static source verdict and its narrower packet limits are separate from transport completion.
